mqtt._comment: Legacy single-broker config. Prefer mqttSources[] for multiple brokers.

mqttSources._comment: WebSocket MQTT broker (e.g. meshcore-mqtt-broker). Use ws:// for plain WebSocket or wss:// for TLS. Username/password supported.
mqttSources.name: wsmqtt

_comment_channelProposals: Shared hashtag channels: visitors suggest public hashtag channels (names only, never keys) on the Channels page. Submissions open only when enabled is true AND apiKey is strong (16+ characters, not a placeholder). By default an administrator approves or rejects suggestions at #/channels?view=proposals with the apiKey. Opt-in autoApprove immediately approves only brand-new names; existing pending, rejected and revoked names are not auto-approved. Approved channels are decrypted by the ingestor and listed for everyone, even before they carry traffic; they stay active if enabled is later set to false. Limits: maxPending/maxApproved bound the table, maxQueuedRequests bounds the request queue next to the database, submissionsPerHour is a global sliding window, and rejected or unreviewed suggestions are deleted after retentionDays. Read by both server and ingestor; changing this policy requires an ingestor restart.
_comment_antennaClaims: Owner antenna heights (#789): a node's owner claims its antenna height with POST /api/nodes/{pubkey}/antenna-claims, gets a 6-character code, puts it into the node's advert name (appended, within the first 23 bytes) and sends an advert. A new advert with a valid signature from that key proves the claim; the code is single-use and expires after 24 h. Claims open only when enabled is true AND apiKey is strong. A proven height waits for an administrator (GET/POST /api/admin/antenna-claims) unless autoApproveProven is true, and even then a height far from the surface estimate waits. Only repeater and room claims with a cached surface estimate can be flagged, so with autoApproveProven on every companion and sensor claim, and every claim whose surface is not cached yet, is approved without review at any height from 0 to 100 m. An approval of a proof older than the node's claim already in force is refused (409). A proven clear removes the owner's height at once. detailsEnabled (#898, default false; needs enabled) also lets owners set station details in the same claim: antenna type, gain (-5 to 20 dBi), power, installation and two optional contacts, contactPublic (shown to everyone on the node page and by GET /api/nodes/{pubkey}/station) and contactAdmin (admin queue only, never public, never logged). A claim that sets details is never auto-approved, and one approval decides the whole claim. Both contacts are deleted when the details are removed, replaced, rejected, revoked or expire, and when retention deletes the claim; admin database backups (GET /api/backup, scripts/backup-sqlite.sh) and SQLite free pages can still hold a deleted contact, because deletion is logical. With detailsEnabled off, setting details is refused (403) but removing them still works. All three switches are read by their exact spelling. Approved heights rank below radio.antennaHeightsM per node and above the surface estimate, and are ignored once the node moves more than staleMoveM (default 50 m, at most 5000) from where the height was proven. reviewDeltaM (default 60 m, at most 1000) is how far above the surface estimate + 2 m a height may be before it is flagged for review (more than 2 m below the surface is always flagged). Limits: maxPending (all nodes) and maxPendingPerNode bound unproven claims (a claim over a limit is refused, never evicts another), maxQueuedRequests bounds the request queue next to the database, submissionsPerHour is a global sliding window, and finished claims are deleted after retentionDays (the approved one is kept). Read by both server and ingestor; changing this policy requires an ingestor restart. Owner page and admin queue (server only, sent to the browser by GET /api/antenna-claims/config): the claim status is checked after pollInitialMs (default 2000, 500-60000), each later wait grows by pollBackoff (default 1.5, 1-4) up to pollMaxMs (default 30000, at most 600000) per wait, for at most pollMaxAttempts checks (default 60, at most 1000) before the page offers Check again; adminDefaultFilter (default proven; pending, approved, rejected, revoked, expired or superseded) is the admin queue's first view. A value out of its range is the default. Owner guide: docs/user-guide/antenna-height-claims.md.

healthThresholds._comment: How long (hours) before nodes show as degraded/silent. 'infra' = repeaters & rooms, 'node' = companions & others. relayActiveHours: a repeater is shown as 'actively relaying' if its pubkey appeared as a path hop in a non-advert packet within this window (issue #662).
healthThresholds._comment_observerThresholds: Observer health classification. Online: last_seen < observerOnlineMinutes ago. Stale: between Online and observerStaleMinutes. Offline: beyond observerStaleMinutes. Defaults 60 / 1440 (1h / 24h) match the node thresholds for consistency and eliminate flap on low-traffic / CDN-fronted instances (#1552). Operators who want the old aggressive 10-min Online threshold can set observerOnlineMinutes: 10.

geo_filter._comment: Optional. By default, also restricts GET /api/nodes (and therefore the live map) to nodes within the polygon + bufferKm — foreign_advert-tagged nodes are always kept regardless (#730, see foreignAdverts below); see geoFilterExemptNodeList to opt out of that. The prune-geo-filter admin flow always uses this polygon regardless of geoFilterExemptNodeList. Polygon is an array of [lat, lon] pairs (minimum 3). Use the GeoFilter tab in the Customizer (requires apiKey) or the GeoFilter Builder (`/geofilter-builder.html`) to draw a polygon visually and export a config snippet. Remove this section to disable filtering entirely. Nodes with no GPS fix are always allowed through.

foreignAdverts._comment: Controls how the ingestor handles ADVERTs whose GPS is OUTSIDE the geo_filter polygon (#730). 'flag' (default): store the advert/node and tag it foreign_advert=1 so operators can see bridged/leaked nodes via the API ('foreign': true on /api/nodes). 'drop': legacy behavior — silently discard the advert (no log, no node row). Only applies when geo_filter is configured; otherwise has no effect.

_comment_geoFilterExemptNodeList: Optional, default false. When geo_filter is configured, GET /api/nodes (and therefore the live map) excludes out-of-polygon nodes by default — the long-standing #730 declutter behavior, preserved automatically for every deployment upgrading from before this field existed. Set to true if you want geo_filter purely for foreign_advert classification/analytics (e.g. a 'Foreign Traffic' investigation) WITHOUT also hiding out-of-polygon nodes from the node list/map. Per-request ?geoFilter=0 / ?geoFilter=1 on /api/nodes overrides either default for a single call. Has no effect on ingestion (foreignAdverts.mode) or the prune-geo-filter admin flow, both of which are unaffected by this flag.
_comment_areas: Optional. GPS-based display filter. Each entry defines a geographic area by polygon ([lat, lon] pairs) or bounding box (latMin/latMax/lonMin/lonMax). Packets and nodes are attributed to an area based on the transmitting node's own GPS coordinates — not the observer's location. Areas appear as a filter pill bar in the dashboard. Remove this section to disable the area filter UI. NOTE: every key under "areas" must be an area object, so this note lives outside the block (#694) — a string in there makes the whole file fail to decode and the server ignores it.
_comment_regionGroups: Optional (#416). Named quick picks over the region codes above: each group renders as one button next to the region filter that selects exactly those codes in one click. Omit the key, or leave it [], and the region filter behaves exactly as it did before the option existed. These are convenience labels over region codes, NOT verified geographic boundaries. Limits: at most 12 groups, at most 24 distinct codes per group, names at most 40 characters. A group that breaks one of those limits, has no name or lists no code is dropped with one log line at startup — a truncated code list or a shortened name would mislabel the filter, so the whole entry is refused instead. Repeated group names (case-insensitive) keep the first one; repeated codes inside a group are de-duplicated. Codes are matched case-insensitively against the served region list (config entries plus every observer IATA in the database), so a code no observer reports is dropped from the group and a group left with no code is not offered at all — an operator can list an observer that is not up yet without creating a dead button. Served by GET /api/config/regions/groups; the flat GET /api/config/regions map is unchanged.

regionPlacement._comment: Optional (server, #488). Which nodes /api/nodes?region= returns. mode: "heard" (default, today's rule) puts a node in every region whose observers heard any of its adverts, so flooded adverts list distant nodes too. "placed" uses direct evidence first: a node is in every region that heard its own transmission (hash count 0 on the observation's own frame; contact re-shares never count), else in the regions that heard it in the fewest relays up to maxHops, else in no region (it stays in the unfiltered list). A legacy row without a stored frame counts an explicit [] path only as a 0-hop fallback. This is an inference from reception, not a verified location. maxHops: cap of the relayed fallback, 0-7, default 3. lifetimeDays: evidence older than this before the node's own newest hearing is ignored, default 30, 0 = no window. persistSpanHours: when set, a region whose direct hearings span less than this is dropped if another region's span at least this (one-off long-distance reception); default 0 = off. Read at startup. Before switching to placed, run the read-only dry-run on a copy of the database: corescope-server -db <copy> -config-dir <dir> -region-placement-dryrun prints counts per basis and region and the unplaced share for several maxHops values, and exits. These values are meant for the customizer in a later release.

cacheTTL._comment_analyticsRF: TTL (seconds) for the shared analytics result cache. Backs /api/analytics/rf, /api/analytics/topology, /api/analytics/distance, /api/analytics/hash-sizes, /api/analytics/channels, /api/analytics/subpaths. Default 60s if unset (#1239) — distance analytics is viewed live during active analysis, so the default smooths cold-miss churn without freezing data. Lower with care; sub-15s values can cause repeated multi-second cold computes during heavy ingest.
cacheTTL._comment: All values in seconds. Server uses these directly. Client fetches via /api/config/cache.

liveMap._comment: How long (ms) to buffer incoming observations of the same packet before animating. Mesh packets propagate through multiple paths and arrive at different observers over several seconds. This window collects all observations of a single transmission so the live map can animate them simultaneously as one realistic propagation event. Set higher for wide meshes with many observers, lower for snappier animations. 5000ms captures ~95% of observations for a typical mesh.
liveMap._comment_maxNodes: Maximum nodes the /live map fetches (and renders) in one page. Default 2000. Raise this on deployments that have measured perf headroom on mid-range mobile (heap + frame-time). Server clamps to [100, 20000]: misconfigured values are coerced silently. Also caps the matching /api/packets?limit fetch the live VCR-rewind code uses. Reporter: #1574.

timestamps._comment: defaultMode: ago|local|iso. timezone: local|utc. formatPreset: iso|us|eu. customFormat: strftime-style (requires allowCustomFormat: true).

packetStore._comment: In-memory packet store. maxMemoryMB caps RAM usage. retentionHours: only packets younger than this are kept in memory (0 = unlimited). hotStartupHours: hours loaded synchronously at startup; background loader fills the remaining retentionHours window. 0 = disabled (loads full retentionHours synchronously, legacy behavior). Set to a positive value (e.g. 24) to reduce startup time on large DBs.
packetStore._comment_gomemlimit: On startup the server reads GOMEMLIMIT from the environment if set; otherwise it derives a Go runtime soft memory limit of maxMemoryMB * 1.5 and applies it via debug.SetMemoryLimit. This forces aggressive GC under cgroup pressure so the process self-throttles before the kernel SIGKILLs it. To override, set GOMEMLIMIT explicitly (e.g. GOMEMLIMIT=850MiB). See issue #836.

runtime._comment_runtime_maxMemoryMB: Go soft memory limit (GOMEMLIMIT) in MiB applied via runtime/debug.SetMemoryLimit at startup. Precedence: GOMEMLIMIT env var > runtime.maxMemoryMB > packetStore.maxMemoryMB-derived (server only). 0 (default) preserves existing behavior. Set on memory-constrained deployments (2 GB Pi, 4 GB VMs) to trigger earlier GC and avoid container OOM-kill. Floor recommendation: ≥1.5× working set; setting below the working set causes a GC death-spiral. Applies to BOTH cmd/server and cmd/ingestor. See #1010.

resolvedPath._comment: How far back (hours) the async backfill scans for observations with NULL resolved_path. Default: 24. Set higher to backfill older data, lower to speed up startup.

_comment_ingestBufferSize: Number of MQTT messages held in memory while the single SQLite writer is blocked by a startup migration/prune (#1608). Drained once the write path is ready; bounded memory (small closure per item). 0 / omit / negative => default 50000 (applied by IngestBufferSizeOrDefault before NewIngestBuffer). A positive value below the default is honored as-is; sub-1 values reaching NewIngestBuffer directly clamp to 1 with a WARN log.
_comment_neighborEdgeCountHalfLifeDays: Ingestor only (#544). OPT-IN and IRREVERSIBLE. 0 / omit / negative = disabled (the default): neighbor_edges.count is a lifetime total that only grows. N > 0 = half-life in days: once per whole day every count is multiplied by 0.5^(1/N) and rounded, never below 3, so old credit (for example bridge TX copies counted before #540) halves every N days and an edge credited r times a day settles near r * 1.44 * N (7 matches the affinity score's half-life). Once enabled, the decayed lifetime counts are gone: setting it back to 0 stops further decay and resets the decay clock, but nothing restores the old counts. Decay changes hop disambiguation: affinity then follows recent traffic, so an edge with large old credit can lose a hop to one with a recent burst. Measure on a copy of your database first with scripts/neighbor-edge-decay-replay.sh. Edges and last_seen never change (retention still decides which edges exist). The stored counts also weight bridge/coverage scores, estimated positions and the GPS sanity check; the neighbour list and neighbour graph are built from packets and are not affected. The clock is stored in the database: missed days are applied after downtime, the first decay is one day after the feature is first enabled, and a clock more than a day in the future is reset. See docs/deployment.md.

neighborGraph._comment: maxAgeDays: neighbor edges older than this many days are pruned on startup and daily. Default 5. maxEdgeKm: geo-implausibility filter — when both endpoints have GPS, edges with haversine distance > maxEdgeKm are rejected at build time to prevent disambiguator self-reinforcement on wide-geo MQTT deployments. Default 500 km (well above any plausible terrestrial LoRa hop). 0 ⇒ use default; set negative to disable the filter. Rejected count surfaces in /api/analytics/neighbor-graph stats. Issue #1228. cacheRecomputeIntervalSeconds: how often the background recomputer refreshes the cached default-shape /api/analytics/neighbor-graph responses (#1481 P0-1). Default 300 (5 min). The graph itself is rebuilt at most once per 5 minutes, so a lower value refreshes the cached responses more often without extra graph-build CPU; a higher value makes the graph older: at most roughly one TTL plus one interval (a non-divisor interval rebuilds every ceil(TTL/interval) ticks, e.g. 90 s gives 360 s). Requests keep the published graph until the next build finishes. Issue #1483, #545.

estimatedPositions._comment: Operator policy for neighbor-derived position estimates. Omit this section or enabled to preserve the default (true). Set false to disable estimates in node details, packet/Ping Scores paths, maps, and estimate-dependent analytics. Reported GPS, ordinary neighbor graphs, and independent IATA/name-based fallbacks are unchanged. Requires a Go server restart and browser refresh; not reloaded by SIGHUP.

observersCache._comment: TTL for the default-shape /api/observers response cache (#1481 P0-3). Default 30s. Lower = fresher data, more SQL pressure on the 1.9M-row observations table. TTL-boundary refills are collapsed via singleflight so concurrent requests cause exactly one SQL fill. Issue #1483.

_comment_knownChannels: Issue #1323. OPT-IN community-maintained hashtag-channels catalogue. Empty string (default) = DISABLED: no background HTTP fetch is started and GET /api/known-channels returns an empty snapshot. To enable, set knownChannelsUrl to a pinned-SHA URL such as "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marcelverdult/meshcore-channels/072bc25b6fc983aa2aa7e9d399a97a5f4899ea71/channels-by-country.json". The URL should point at the channels-by-country.json shape: {generated_at, license, countries:{cc:[{channel,description,key?}]}}. Always pin to a specific commit SHA (not the moving 'main' branch) so a hostile or compromised future upstream commit cannot be silently fetched by your deployment; periodically bump the pin after reviewing upstream diffs. Fetched in the background every knownChannelsRefreshMs (default 86400000 = 24h). Stored in-memory only — no DB, no disk cache. Surfaced over GET /api/known-channels?region=XX. Cache is fail-soft: a failed refresh keeps the last-known snapshot in place. No credentials are sent.

batteryThresholds._comment: Voltage cutoffs (millivolts) for the per-node battery trend chart on /node-analytics. Latest sample below lowMv shows the node as ⚠️ Low; below criticalMv shows 🪫 Critical. Both default to 3300 / 3000 if omitted. Source data: observer_metrics.battery_mv populated from observer status messages; only nodes that are themselves observers (matching pubkey ↔ observer id) yield a series. Issue #663.

_comment_dutyCycleWarnPct: TX airtime share (percent) over the last hour at which RF Health and the observer list flag an observer. Default 10, the EU 868 MHz g3 sub-band limit; raise it (e.g. 50) elsewhere. Repeater firmware defaults to a 50% budget (airtime_factor 1.0), so the device does not enforce this itself. Issue #479.
_comment_mqttSources: Each source connects to an MQTT broker. Supported schemes: mqtt:// (plain TCP), mqtts:// (TLS), ws:// (WebSocket), wss:// (WebSocket TLS). topics: what to subscribe to. iataFilter: only ingest packets from these regions (optional). region: default IATA region for this source — used when packet/topic doesn't specify one (optional, priority: payload > topic > this field). clientId: MQTT client ID, used verbatim (optional; must be unique among the broker's concurrent clients, and at most 23 characters of [0-9A-Za-z] for strict MQTT 3.1 brokers). When omitted, each ingestor start generates corescope-<name>-<8 random hex>, so copies of this file never share an ID — do not add a fixed clientId here.
_comment_compression: Opt-in HTTP gzip middleware + WebSocket permessage-deflate. Both default to false — enable ONLY when your upstream reverse proxy is NOT already compressing. gzip: enables the gzipMiddleware wrapper around the HTTP handler. websocket: sets gorilla websocket Upgrader.EnableCompression. level: gzip compression level 1..9 (1=BestSpeed, 9=BestCompression, default 6). minSizeBytes: advisory minimum response size below which compression would not pay off. contentTypes: MIME allow-list — only responses with these Content-Type values are compressed. Already-compressed types (image/*, video/*, audio/*, application/zip, application/x-gzip, application/pdf, application/octet-stream) are always skipped, as are responses whose handler already set Content-Encoding. Omit contentTypes to use the built-in default allow-list.
_comment_clientRegions: Opt-in declared-region reports (#126): a mobile companion asks a repeater in direct range which regions it lets flood and relays the answer on meshcore/client/<pubkey>/regions; each answer is kept as a report in client_declared_regions with its collector, reported time, ingest time and the repeater's own clock. Default OFF and independent of clientRxCoverage. SINGLE FLAG, BOTH PROCESSES: it gates the ingest write path and GET /api/nodes/{pubkey}/declared-regions (404 when off), which serves reports without collector keys or positions. The clientRxCoverage.sources allowlist and observerBlacklist apply to this topic too. TRUST: requires a broker ACL binding meshcore/client/{pubkey}/regions to that publisher; target and regions are the collector's claim, never authoritative. Retention: retention.clientRegionsDays. Erasure: admin delete-client-rx also deletes the reports a key collected. See docs/client-regions.md.
_comment_moments: Live "Moments" (#881): the server detects a few noteworthy events and broadcasts them on the WebSocket as {"type":"moment"}; GET /api/moments lists the newest. Default OFF: no detector runs, nothing is broadcast and /api/moments returns an empty list. Kinds: new_node (a repeater, room or sensor key first seen in retained history), back_online (a repeater heard again after at least backOnlineHours of silence; 24 = 2x the firmware's 12 h flood-advert default), record_link (a new longest confident direct neighbor link inside the rolling recordWindowHours, at least recordMinKm and at most neighborGraph.maxEdgeKm), busiest_repeater (most distinct non-advert relays in the last busyWindowMinutes, at least busyMinRelays). Detection runs on existing timers only (node delta every 15 s, neighbor-graph reload every 60 s, the relay recompute), never per packet. maxPerMinute is the global rate (burst 3) on top of fixed per-kind caps; historySize is how many moments /api/moments keeps (in memory, lost on restart). Companions never appear; nodeBlacklist, observerBlacklist, hiddenNamePrefixes and the node-list geo_filter apply; positions are advertised GPS only. Ranges: backOnlineHours 1-720, recordWindowHours 1-168, recordMinKm 0.1-1000, busyWindowMinutes 1-1440, busyMinRelays 1-1000000, maxPerMinute 1-60, historySize 1-500; out-of-range values are clamped with a log line, 0 or missing takes the default.
_comment_clientRxCoverage: Opt-in mobile client-RX coverage (corescope-rx companions publishing GPS-tagged receptions to meshcore/client/<pubkey>/packets). Default OFF: when disabled the ingestor writes no client_receptions, the /api/rx-coverage|rx-leaderboard|nodes/{pubkey}/rx-coverage endpoints 404, and the UI hides the Coverage dashboard + Reach overlay. Set enabled=true to turn it on. SINGLE FLAG, BOTH PROCESSES: the ingestor and server each parse this same config.json, so this one clientRxCoverage.enabled entry gates both the ingest write path and the read endpoints — set it once, not per-process. TRUST: the feature requires an ACL-capable broker binding meshcore/client/{pubkey}/packets to that publisher; without ACLs the companion GPS is spoofable (see docs/client-rx-coverage.md). Retention: see retention.clientRxDays. Companion app + setup: https://github.com/efiten/corescope-rx.
_comment_clientRxCoverage_sources: OPTIONAL allow-list of mqttSources[].name entries that may contribute client RX coverage. Omitted or empty (the default) = every source is accepted, unchanged behaviour. Set it when this instance reads MORE THAN ONE broker and they do not all bind meshcore/client/<pubkey>/packets to the publisher holding that key: coverage is only as trustworthy as the weakest broker, so on a mixed deployment (one broker with per-device identity + one legacy username/password broker where many accounts may write meshcore/#) any account on the weak broker could otherwise inject coverage under any companion pubkey with any GPS position. Listing the trusted source names keeps the client namespace on those sources — a client message from any other source is dropped before any write (no client_receptions, no client_observers, no observer row), logged per source with throttling and a line cap. Matching is on the source name, trimmed and case-insensitive; a source with no name can never be listed. A name matching no configured source is logged once at startup. Example: "clientRxCoverage": { "enabled": true, "sources": ["device-auth"] }. See docs/client-rx-coverage.md.
_comment_channelKeys: Hex keys for decrypting channel messages. Key name = channel display name. public channel key is well-known.
_comment_hashChannels: Channel names whose keys are derived via SHA256. Key = SHA256(name)[:16]. Listed here so the ingestor can auto-derive keys.
_comment_hashRegions: Region names for scope matching on transport-route packets. Key = SHA256('#name')[:16]. Add any region names used by nodes in your network.
_comment_hashRegionsPath: OPTIONAL path to an external JSON file holding region names as a plain array, e.g. ["dk", "dk-aarhus"] (issue #360). Omitted or empty (the default) = inline hashRegions only, exactly as before; there is no auto-discovered default file. When set, the effective set is the UNION of the inline hashRegions list above and the file, normalized the same way ('#' prefix added, whitespace trimmed, blank entries dropped) and deduplicated after normalization. Set it when the region list is large and machine-maintained: a real deployment carries ~1100 names, which is a third of config.json once hashChannels and areas are counted, and moving it out makes the rest reviewable. SINGLE KEY, BOTH PROCESSES: the ingestor (which derives one HMAC key per region) and the server (which reports unknown scopes in Observer Neighbors and unusedRegions in /api/scope-stats) read it through the same loader, so they cannot disagree about which scopes are configured. A RELATIVE path resolves against the directory holding THIS config.json, never the process working directory, so both processes find the same file. Env override: HASH_REGIONS_PATH, which wins over this key. If the path is set but the file is missing or not a JSON array of strings, the error is logged and the inline hashRegions list is used; on the ingestor's SIGHUP reload the previous keys are kept instead. A SIGHUP re-reads the file, so adding a region needs no restart. Names are case-sensitive: "#dk" and "#DK" are different scopes with different keys.
_comment_defaultRegion: IATA code shown by default in region filters.
_comment_mapDefaults: Initial map center [lat, lon] and zoom level.
_comment_regions: IATA code → display name mapping for the region filter UI. Each key is a 3-letter IATA code that an observer is tagged with (resolved priority: MQTT payload `region` field > topic-derived region > mqttSources.region). Observers without an IATA tag will not appear under any region filter — only under 'All Regions'. The region filter dropdown shows one entry per code listed here PLUS any extra IATA codes the server discovers from observers at runtime (so you can omit codes here and they will still be selectable, just labelled with the bare IATA code instead of a friendly name). Selecting 'All Regions' (or no region) returns results from every observer including those with no IATA tag; selecting one or more codes restricts results to packets observed by observers tagged with those codes. The reserved value 'All' (case-insensitive) is treated as 'no filter' on the server, so the URL ?region=All behaves identically to omitting the param. Issue #770.

analytics._comment_pauseWhenIdle: Issue #492. Opt-in, default false (every analytics snapshot is recomputed on its interval whether read or not). When true, a scheduled recompute is skipped if nothing read that endpoint's default snapshot since the previous recompute, so an instance whose analytics pages are rarely open stops recomputing and allocating for them. Freshness trade-off: the first read after a pause is served the existing snapshot at once — it can be much older than the interval — and wakes one refresh; reads after that see fresh data. While pauseWhenIdle is on, responses served from a snapshot carry X-Analytics-Snapshot (current|stale) and X-Analytics-Snapshot-Age-Seconds, so a stale snapshot is never presented as freshly computed. Startup load, warm-up gates and failed recomputes are unaffected: a recomputer only pauses after a successful pass that started once the startup load finished.

loraPreset._comment_: Issue #1768. LoRa PHY preset assumed by the Relay Airtime Share metric to compute true Time-on-Air. Share numbers are only meaningful relative to one preset, so operators MUST set this to match their mesh — freq is informational (surfaces in the chart caption) and does not affect ToA; bw is bandwidth in kHz (e.g. 62.5, 125, 250); sf is spreading factor (6..12); cr is the denominator of the 4/N coding rate (5 ⇒ 4/5 … 8 ⇒ 4/8). Defaults reproduce the typical EU MeshCore deployment 869.6 MHz / BW 62.5 kHz / SF 8 / CR 4/5. CRC=1, IH=0, DE (T_sym ≥ 16 ms), and preamble (32 for SF≤8, 16 otherwise, per firmware preambleLengthForSF) are firmware-fixed and intentionally not exposed as config.

_comment_analytics: Issue #1240 + #1256 + #1265. Each analytics endpoint (topology, rf, distance, channels, hashCollisions, hashSizes, roles, observersClockSkew, nodesClockSkew, advertIntervals) is recomputed in the background on the configured interval and served from an atomic-pointer cache. Reads never block on compute. Default 300s (5 min) per endpoint reflects the operator principle: serving slightly stale data quickly beats real-time data slowly. Lower values = fresher data at higher CPU cost. Only the default query (no region/window) is precomputed; region- and window-filtered requests fall back to the legacy on-request compute + 60s TTL cache.

customizer._comment_disabledTabs: Issue #1508. List of customizer-modal tab ids to hide from end users. Useful when operators want to expose only daily-use viewer controls and keep one-shot admin chrome out of the way. Recognized ids: branding, theme, nodes, home, display, geofilter, export. Example: ["branding", "geofilter", "export"] hides the admin tabs and leaves theme/colors/home/display visible. Default [] keeps the legacy behavior (all tabs visible). Operators edit this in config.json directly — there is no in-app UI for this list (by design).

privacy._comment: Opt-in privacy-notice page at #/privacy. Default off; set enabled=true to publish the page and the nav links that point at it. This flag is the ENTIRE privacy configuration -- the notice itself is a FIXED document in public/privacy.js and is deliberately not operator-editable, so the published wording cannot drift from the notice that was reviewed and signed off. Nothing you can put in config.json adds, removes or rewords a single line of it; changing the notice means editing that file. Older configs may still contain the removed text fields (controllerName, purposesText, retentionText and the rest) -- they are ignored, not rejected. None of this is legal advice, and publishing the page does not by itself make a deployment compliant.
